rows.context: 211.82 Receipt and storage of untested components, drug product containers, and closures.
rows.text: Upon receipt and before acceptance, each container or grouping of containers of components, drug product containers, and closures shall be examined visually for appropriate labeling as to contents, container damage or broken seals, and contamination.

passages.text:
1. Purpose

To describe how raw materials, containers and closures are received, held in quarantine, sampled, tested and released or rejected.

3. Receipt

3.1 Each delivery is checked against the purchase order. Every container is examined for damage, broken seals and contamination, and the result is written on the goods receipt note. 3.2 Each lot receives an internal receipt number, and every container is labelled with it and with the status QUARANTINE. 3.3 Quarantined material is stored off the floor, in the yellow-lined quarantine area, until QC releases it.

4. Sampling

4.1 QC samples a statistically chosen number of containers of each lot (the square root of the number of containers plus one). 4.2 Containers are opened only in the sampling booth and resealed, and each sampled container is marked. 4.3 The sample containers are labelled with the material name, receipt number, the container it came from, the date and the name of the sampler.

rows.text: Components, drug product containers, and closures shall be stored under quarantine until they have been tested or examined, whichever is appropriate, and released.

passages.text:

For the other specification tests, the supplier's certificate of analysis may be accepted once QC has qualified the supplier and confirms the certificate's results at least once a year. 5.2 Containers and closures are tested against their drawings. 5.3 QC changes the status label to RELEASED or REJECTED. Rejected lots are moved to the locked reject cage.

6. Use and retest

Released material is issued first in, first out. A lot past its retest date is held and retested before use.
